title: Kaplan–Meier Estimator & Log-rank Test
interviewAnswer: Kaplan–Meier estimates the survival curve nonparametrically by multiplying conditional survival probabilities at event times. The log-rank test compares survival curves across groups under assumptions.
keyPoints: Median survival comes from S(t)=0.5 when reached.
Curves can cross, complicating simple comparisons.
why: Kaplan–Meier Estimator & Log-rank Test appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Kaplan–Meier estimates the survival curve nonparametrically by multiplying conditional survival probabilities at event times. The log-rank test compares survival curves across groups under assumptions. Median survival comes from S(t)=0.5 when reached. Curves can cross, complicating simple comparisons. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Compare retention survival for two acquisition channels while accounting for recent users who have not yet churned.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Kaplan–Meier Estimator & Log-rank Test make?
How would you validate or debug Kaplan–Meier Estimator & Log-rank Test in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

lab.goal: Fit and inspect a Kaplan–Meier survival curve.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
t=np.array([1,2,2,3,5],float); e=np.array([1,1,0,1,0])
s=1.0
for time in sorted(set(t[e==1])):
    at_risk=(t>=time).sum(); events=((t==time)&(e==1)).sum(); s*=1-events/at_risk
    print(time,s)
lab.shipIt: Production survival dashboards should define event/censoring rules, cohort entry, timezone/window semantics and delayed labels explicitly.
